---
title: "Global Stress: P-Norm Aggregation for Stress Constraints"
toc: true
---

## Description

This tutorial demonstrates topology optimization with global stress constraints
using p-norm aggregation. Instead of constraining stress at every element
(thousands of constraints), we aggregate von Mises stresses into a single
global measure using the p-norm with p=5. This approach enables efficient
gradient-based optimization while controlling peak stresses.

The tutorial optimizes volume fraction minimization subject to a stress
threshold, demonstrating stress-driven design for cantilever and Half MBB
benchmarks.

## Setup

```{julia}
#| output: false
using TopOpt, LinearAlgebra
```

## Define the Problem

```{julia}
#| output: false
E = 1.0 # Young's modulus
v = 0.3 # Poisson's ratio
f = 1.0 # downward force
rmin = 3.0 # filter radius

problems = Any[
    PointLoadCantilever(Val{:Linear}, (60, 20), (1.0, 1.0), E, v, f),
    HalfMBB(Val{:Linear}, (60, 20), (1.0, 1.0), E, v, f),
]
problem_names = ["Cantilever beam", "Half MBB beam"]

i = 1  # Select problem (1 or 2)
println(problem_names[i])
problem = problems[i]
```

## Parameter Settings

```{julia}
#| output: false
V = 0.5 # volume fraction
xmin = 0.001 # minimum density
convcriteria = Nonconvex.KKTCriteria()
penalty = PowerPenalty(1.0)  # start with no penalization

solver = FEASolver(DirectSolver, problem; xmin=xmin, penalty=penalty)
```

## Stress Objective

```{julia}
#| output: false
# von Mises stress function (automatically differentiable via Zygote)
stress = von_mises_stress_function(solver)

filter = if problem isa TopOptProblems.TieBeam
    identity
else
    DensityFilterFun(solver; rmin=rmin)
end

volfrac = VolumeFun(solver)
comp = ComplianceFun(solver)

x0 = ones(length(solver.vars))
# Stress threshold: 2× the initial peak stress of the fully-solid design
threshold = 2 * maximum(stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x0))))

# Minimize volume with a compliance regularization term. The regularizer
# steers the optimizer toward stiff layouts, preventing the trivial
# all-void solution that pure volume minimization would produce.
λ = 1e-4
obj = x -> volfrac(filter(PseudoDensities(x))) + λ * comp(filter(PseudoDensities(x)))
constr = x -> norm(stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x))), 5) - threshold
```

The p-norm with p=5 aggregates element stresses into a global measure:
`‖σ‖₅ = (Σ σᵢ⁵)^(1/5)`. This smooth approximation enables efficient gradient
computation while capturing peak stress behavior. The threshold is set just
above the initial peak stress so the constraint stays active throughout
optimization. The compliance regularizer (`λ·uᵀKu`) penalizes overly
compliant (near-void) designs, keeping the optimization away from the
degenerate empty-domain solution.

## Optimization Setup

```{julia}
#| output: false
N = length(solver.vars)
x0 = fill(0.5, N)

model = Model(obj)
addvar!(model, zeros(N), ones(N))
add_ineq_constraint!(model, constr)
alg = MMA87()
```

## Continuation Strategy

Volume minimization with a loose stress constraint collapses to the trivial
all-void design. We ramp the SIMP penalty exponent from 1.0 to 3.0 so the
optimizer must commit material to satisfy the stress constraint, with
decaying KKT tolerances for accurate subproblem solves:

```{julia}
#| output: false
ps = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
tols = [1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4]

x = copy(x0)
```

## Run Optimization

```{julia}
#| output: true
for j in eachindex(ps)
    global x, convcriteria
    p = ps[j]
    tol = tols[j]
    setpenalty!(solver, p)
    options = MMAOptions(; maxiter=50, tol=Tolerance(; kkt=tol), convcriteria)
    r = optimize(model, alg, x; options)
    global x = r.minimizer
    println("Step $j: penalty=$p, tol=$tol, obj=$(obj(x)), constr=$(constr(x))")
end
```

## Results

```{julia}
#| output: true
@show obj(r.minimizer)
@show constr(r.minimizer)
```

The optimized design minimizes material usage while keeping aggregated stress
below the threshold.

## Visualization

```{julia}
#| label: fig-global-stress
#| fig-cap: "Global stress-constrained optimization with p-norm aggregation (p=5)"
using CairoMakie
fig = visualize(problem; topology=r.minimizer)

```
